key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines thermal simulation and AI surrogates to screen robotic welding conditions and control strategies before in-space testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive welding control for future on-orbit assembly and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates approximate weld-model outputs.
Simulated UR5 welding uses proportional power-setting control as travel speed drops near a seam corner.
evidence_signal: GPs outperformed neural networks across eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
